D9·hwcd — 2026-09-16
rule: Every execution of candidate code — the agent, the candidate sofar, its build, the agent-written app's build and tests — runs under the evaluator's sandbox profile, and a result is written only by the evaluator process after the pin, the sandbox self-test and both controls hold; never score a candidate with any sofar binary or from any text the agent wrote.
chose: 3.1 contract — the FROZEN EVALUATOR, settled before code. (1) SEPARATE REPO AND PROCESS: the evaluator lives in ~/IO/sofar-evaluator (own local git, bun + TypeScript, zero deps), never in sofar (the candidate's repo) and never in handoff-bench (the live round-1 runner a peer session edits). Results land under ~/IO/bench-cells/evaluator/<run>/, written only by the evaluator process. No sofar binary — candidate or installed — ever interprets a result (audit S4: the candidate may be the supervising binary). (2) THE MEASUREMENT PATH IS PINNED, NOT TRUSTED: PIN.json names the handoff-bench commit plus sha256 of every file the evaluator uses (hidden-tests/** incl. vendor fixtures, CHAIN-A.md, runner/lib/{agents,arms,billing,cell,chain,mcp,paths,proc}.ts, runner package.json + bun.lock), the skeleton commit efc0137 and its tree hash, the chain-A reference commit 65a98ca, the sandbox profiles' hashes, and the tool versions (bun, node, claude, macOS, sandbox-exec present). Every run re-verifies all of it and REFUSES (exit 2, a refusal record, nothing else) on any hash mismatch, a missing or added file, a dirty working copy of a pinned path, or a tool version change — naming the first offender. (3) THE CANDIDATE RUNS INSIDE A KERNEL SANDBOX, AND SO DOES EVERY BYTE OF ITS CODE: macOS sandbox-exec (Seatbelt) profile `candidate.sb`: (allow default), (deny file-write*) with an allow-list {the cell directory, the bench agent profile ~/.bench/claude-config, ~/.local/state/sofar, /private/tmp, /private/var/folders, /dev}, (deny file-read*) on {hidden-tests, ~/IO/bench-sealed, the chain-A reference, the evaluator results, the evaluator repo}, and (deny process-exec /bin/launchctl). It applies to the agent (`claude` reached through a PATH shim that exec's sandbox-exec), to the candidate `sofar` (its bin entry IS such a shim), to `sofar init` during cell setup, and to the candidate's own build during `pack`. The agent-written app's `bun install`/`build` and the hidden-test run execute under a second profile `score.sb` (writes: the cell repo, tmp, the junit outfile only) because an agent-authored build script is candidate code too. (4) ISOLATION IS MEASURED AT EVERY RUN: before any launch the evaluator runs a self-test inside candidate.sb — write hidden-tests, write results, read harness.ts, read bench-sealed, exec launchctl must ALL fail with EPERM and a write into the cell must succeed — and refuses to launch otherwise. Verified 2026-09-16 on macOS 27.0: write allow-list, rm/mv/chmod, symlink escape, sealed read and nested profiles all enforce. (5) CANDIDATE IDENTITY IS THE ARTIFACT, NOT THE BRANCH: `pack` exports one git commit with `git archive`, builds and `npm pack`s sofar.sh inside the sandbox, and names the candidate `cand-<sha256(tarball)[0:12]>`; the result carries the commit, the tarball hash and the package version; the install lives under bench-cells/evaluator/candidates (write-denied to the candidate). (6) CONTROLS PROVE THE EVALUATOR CAN SEE PASS AND FAIL: per pin, the requested sessions' hidden tests are run against the chain-A reference (every test must pass) and the skeleton (each session must fail at least one test); a candidate score is refused until both controls hold for the current pin. (7) SCORES ARE READ FROM THE TRUSTED PROCESS, CROSS-CHECKED: the junit file is written to a random per-run name, parsed by the evaluator, and must agree with the `bun test` exit code and stdout summary; a filter that ran zero tests is `no_tests_ran`, never a pass; disagreement is `score_inconsistent` and refused. The agent's own text is never a score. (8) EVERY LAUNCH IS RECORDED BEFORE IT HAPPENS: attempts.jsonl gets a row before and after each agent launch with usage and reported cost, the seed 3.2's durable ledger sums; a billing/limit signal (bench-refresh D14 patterns) stops the run with exit 3. (9) THE HOLDOUT IS UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION: the evaluator re-execs ITSELF under `evaluator.sb`, which denies reading ~/IO/bench-sealed, so the development loop cannot touch chain B even by bug. (10) STATED LIMITS: everything runs as one uid, so the boundary covers the process tree the evaluator launches and nothing the operator starts outside it; sandbox-exec is deprecated by Apple though enforced today; the candidate can read most of the machine (only sealed paths are read-denied) and reach the network; a candidate could still plant persistence through IPC the profile does not name. The one handoff-bench change is `BENCH_SOFAR_PREFIX` as an env override of the pinned prefix in runner/lib/paths.ts, default unchanged, so the live round is untouched (bench-refresh D5).
over: A checksum plus a final diff of hidden-tests/*.ts (the audit's S4 straw man); chmod a-w on the evaluator tree (same uid can chmod back); a second unix account (real isolation, but needs sudo and an interactive setup the operator has not granted — kept as a later hardening); putting the evaluator inside the sofar repo or its packages (the candidate's write surface); reusing the round-1 runner's run.ts/ledger.ts/modes.ts (dirty in a peer's tree, and its caps are 3.2's job); swapping the contents of ~/.bench/sofar-0.32.0 to point at a candidate (audit S6: never swap the installed sofar under a running benchmark); trusting the junit file alone (the app under test runs inside the same score sandbox and could write it).
because: Audit S4 asks for a frozen supervisor and evaluator outside the candidate's write/control surface with the whole measurement path pinned, known-good/known-bad controls, and tamper fixtures — and says to pick a mechanism that actually enforces the boundary and to state remaining limits honestly. sandbox-exec is the only enforcement available to this uid without sudo, and its behaviour was tested rather than assumed. Pinning by content hash rather than by commit alone catches uncommitted edits in the live runner tree; pinning only the files the evaluator uses lets it run while a peer's round-orchestration edits are dirty. Sandboxing every execution of candidate code, not just the agent, closes the `sofar init`, pack-time build and agent-authored build-script paths that a checksum never sees. The self-test at every run turns the isolation claim into a per-run measurement, in the same spirit as session-driver D8's settings read-back.
